einzeiler: Exploring the origins, plot, and complete incidental music of Grieg's Peer Gynt
kurzfassung: Edvard Grieg composed nearly two hours of incidental music for Henrik Ibsen's surreal play Peer Gynt, far exceeding the famous suites known today. Joshua Weilerstein examines the dramatic plot alongside Grieg's complete score, revealing hidden choral parts and surprising stylistic depths. The episode uncovers how Grieg's rich orchestration and emotional range bring Ibsen's complex protagonist and tragic heroines to life.
stichpunkte: Edvard Grieg wrote nearly two hours of incidental music for Henrik Ibsen's play Peer Gynt, though only a fraction is commonly performed in suites.
Ibsen's sprawling, innovative play mixes reality and fantasy, following the antihero Peer Gynt from Norway to North Africa and back.
Grieg took the commission primarily because he was broke, despite initially disliking the play.
The full score features surprising elements like troll choruses and Wagnerian parodies that are absent from standard orchestral suites.
Characters like Ingrid and Solveig receive surprisingly empathetic and tender musical treatment amidst Peer's chaotic journey.
Grieg's famous pieces like Morning Mood and In the Hall of the Mountain King take on entirely new meanings within their original theatrical contexts.
The final acts delve into heavy existential themes as an aging Peer is forced to account for his wasted life before finding solace with Solveig.

clips.hook: Composing nearly two hours of music
clips.text: The two standard suites last around 45 minutes, but the composer originally created almost 105 minutes of music for the production.
The title character is introduced as an alcoholic pretender who spends his time telling tall tales and drawing the ire of his mother.
Most listeners have never heard the famous Mountain King theme performed with its original choral accompaniment sung by trolls.

clips.hook: Beating The Nutcracker to the punch
clips.text: Anitra's Dance predates Tchaikovsky's famous ballet score, proving that Grieg embraced exoticism long before similar late-19th-century works.
Inanimate objects like balls of yarn and dead leaves confront the protagonist to tell him that he is essentially nothing.

beschreibung: Grieg's Peer Gynt suites are among the best-known and best-loved works of classical music in the world. They are practically embedded into popular culture, being used in a dizzying number of cartoons, advertisements, and films. In the classical music world, as with Beethoven's 5th symphony, they have almost become a cliché, and they are often performed on so-called Pops concerts. The two big hits from Peer Gynt, Morning Mood and In the Hall of the Mountain King, are instantly recognizable to the general public, even if they don't know who wrote the music or where it comes from. And where all this music comes from is really interesting, and is going to be one of the main topics of this show. Because the famous music from Peer Gynt comes from the two suites that Grieg took from his massive score of incidental music to Henrik Ibsen's play in verse, Peer Gynt. The two suites together take about 45 minutes to perform, but Grieg actually wrote an extra hour's worth of music! He then extracted, for his suites, the music that he felt would stand on its own without the text, and this was quite a good decision, as they are certainly his most popular pieces and have etched his name into the classical music pantheon forever. But what about the rest of that music? What about the play itself? Today, on this Patreon-sponsored episode, we'll tell the story of the origins of Peer Gynt, both from Ibsen and from Grieg, and then we'll go through the nearly 2 hours of incidental music, most of it in a bit of a cursory way (which frankly is perfectly appropriate for Grieg, whose music abounds with naive simplicity and gorgeous tunes), but all the way through we are going to tell the wacky, wonderful, and way-ahead-of-its-time story of Peer Gynt, all through the music that Grieg wrote. On the show today you'll hear some of the most famous music in the world, and then some music that only the most passionate of connoisseurs have encountered. So, in essence, my kind of show. Join us!
